description: Gurkha Signals is a Nepal-based team of builders, developers, and problem-solvers passionate about using NASA data, technology, and science to uncover hidden patterns in Earth's changing systems. We combine software, data analysis, AI, and scientific thinking to turn complex Earth-system data into meaningful insights.
summary:
Safe Field Nepal is a mobile-first decision-support app that helps Nepali smallholder farmers decide when to irrigate, fertilize, or spray and when to wait using NASA Earth observations they would otherwise never see.

It turns NASA data into seven plain-language field signals: rainfall from GPM IMERG, soil moisture from SMAP L4, land-surface temperature from VIIRS, vegetation greenness from MODIS/VIIRS, and air temperature from NASA POWER, combined with open forecasts and soil texture. Every number shows its source, date, resolution, and whether it is live, cached, or stale; when clouds or latency make a signal unreliable, the app says so instead of guessing. Farmers also get a fertilizer and pesticide safety guide, an irrigation planner, and full Nepali/English support that works offline. Field boundaries never leave the phone.

This matters because fertilizer timing and irrigation drive both yield and runoff pollution in Nepal, yet most farmers have no access to satellite insight.
details:
Safe Field Nepal – Making Agricultural Data Easier to Understand, One Field at a Time

Website link:
Safe Field Nepal is a Nepal-focused agricultural research prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

Our project explores how NASA satellite observations, environmental datasets, and geospatial technologies can help Nepalese farmers better understand the environmental conditions surrounding their agricultural land.

What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

Farmers often make important agricultural decisions, such as when to apply fertilizer, spray pesticides, or carry out field activities, using years of experience, visual observations, and their understanding of local weather patterns. However, reliable environmental information is not always accessible or easy to interpret at an individual farm level.

Safe Field Nepal addresses this challenge by bringing multiple environmental data sources together into one location-aware platform.

Farmers can select their land by tapping on an interactive map, using their phone's GPS while standing in the field, walking around the field corners, or drawing their field boundary manually. Once a location is selected, the platform retrieves available environmental information relevant to that geographical area.

The application integrates:

  • NASA GPM IMERG: Satellite-based rainfall estimates for exploring recent precipitation patterns.
  • NASA POWER: Historical and regional climate information for understanding environmental trends.
  • NASA SMAP: Soil moisture observations and estimates for understanding surface and root-zone moisture conditions.
  • NASA VIIRS: Land-surface temperature and vegetation-related datasets.
  • ISRIC SoilGrids: Modelled soil-texture information, including sand, silt, and clay fractions.
  • Open-Meteo: Short-term weather forecasts and past-days rainfall information.
  • Elevation and terrain data: Geographic context for understanding elevation and estimated slope.

These datasets are processed through a Python-based backend and presented through an interactive, mobile-first dashboard. The platform also provides preliminary environmental screening labels, farm records, and an AI-assisted, plain-language field question interface.

Users can explore the information in English or Nepali and listen to assistant responses using device-based speech synthesis.

What Benefits Does It Have?

Safe Field Nepal aims to make complex environmental and satellite information more approachable for ordinary farmers.

Its main benefits include:

  1. Location-specific exploration: Farmers can explore environmental information associated with their selected agricultural land instead of relying only on general regional reports.
  2. Better environmental awareness: Rainfall, soil-texture estimates, moisture, weather forecasts, and terrain information are available in one place.
  3. More informed decisions: Farmers can use available environmental evidence alongside their own experience when considering agricultural activities.
  4. Accessibility: English and Nepali language support, mobile-first design, and read-aloud functionality make information easier to access.
  5. Improved data transparency: Each displayed measurement identifies its source, date, data type, and freshness, helping users distinguish observations, forecasts, modelled estimates, fallback data, and cached information.
  6. Offline awareness: Recently cached assessments can remain accessible when an internet connection is unavailable, with their original timestamps preserved.

What Is the Intended Impact?

Our intended impact is to reduce the gap between advanced Earth observation technology and the everyday information needs of Nepalese farming communities.

Nepal has diverse geographical conditions, from the Terai plains to the hills and mountainous regions. Agricultural conditions can vary considerably across relatively short distances. We therefore believe that making environmental information easier to explore at individual field locations can be a valuable step toward more informed and climate-aware agriculture.

We initially focus on Nepal, with particular attention to the pilot districts of Morang, Sunsari, Jhapa, and Ilam.

In the longer term, we hope to develop Safe Field Nepal into a more comprehensive agricultural intelligence platform that supports farmers, agricultural researchers, and local communities through accessible environmental information.

What Technologies and Tools Did We Use?

We developed the project using a combination of modern web technologies, scientific computing tools, satellite-data processing libraries, and open environmental datasets.

Frontend:

  • Next.js
  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • MapLibre GL JS
  • Recharts
  • Lucide React

Backend and scientific processing:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pydantic
  • Uvicorn
  • NumPy
  • SciPy
  • Statsmodels
  • pymannkendall

Geospatial and satellite-data processing:

  • NASA Earthdata access tools (earthaccess)
  • xarray
  • netCDF4
  • Shapely
  • pyproj

Data storage and infrastructure:

  • SQLite
  • Supabase PostgreSQL and Storage (optional)
  • GitHub and GitHub Actions
  • Netlify for frontend deployment
  • Render for backend hosting

The project uses publicly available NASA and other open environmental datasets rather than relying on simulated environmental measurements.

How Is the Project Creative and Innovative?

Our creativity lies in translating complex Earth observation data into an experience designed around an actual farmer's field rather than a scientific dashboard.

Instead of requiring users to understand satellite products, geographical grids, or scientific measurements, we allow them to start with something familiar: selecting their own land on a map.

We also considered the human side of agricultural decision-making during our preliminary research. Before the NASA Space Apps hackathon, we interviewed a farmer to understand how agricultural activities are planned using observations of the sky, clouds, and surrounding environmental conditions. This helped us recognize the importance of connecting scientific information with farmers' practical experiences.

Some distinctive aspects of our approach include:

  • Combining multiple NASA satellite products and environmental datasets in one field-oriented platform.
  • Providing multiple ways to identify agricultural land, including GPS averaging and field-boundary mapping.
  • Separating real observations, modelled estimates, forecasts, and fallback information instead of presenting them as interchangeable measurements.
  • Introducing bilingual interaction and read-aloud responses to reduce language and accessibility barriers.
  • Designing automated satellite-data ingestion, validation, caching, and retention workflows.
  • Displaying unavailable or insufficient-quality data honestly rather than filling missing measurements with invented values.

We believe that transparency is as important as innovation when developing technology intended to support agricultural decisions.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Throughout development, we considered several important factors:

1. Nepal's geographical diversity: The platform needed to account for differences in terrain, elevation, and environmental conditions across Nepal.

2. Farmers' accessibility: We prioritized a mobile-first interface, simple workflows, English and Nepali language support, and accessible explanations.

3. Scientific reliability: Satellite datasets have different spatial resolutions, update frequencies, coverage, and uncertainties. We designed the application to preserve data provenance and communicate these limitations.

4. Real-world agricultural practices: Our preliminary farmer interview helped us understand the importance of local experience and practical decision-making.

5. Data availability: NASA products are not always published immediately or available at the same frequency. Our system accounts for publication delays, missing data, quality checks, and cached information.

6. Privacy: Field boundaries remain on the farmer's device, and precise field coordinates are not included in application logs.

7. Scalability and sustainability: We designed a modular backend, automated data-refresh workflows, and flexible storage so that the platform can evolve as additional datasets and capabilities become available.

8. Responsible use: Safe Field Nepal is currently an educational research prototype, not a scientifically validated agricultural advisory service. Its screening thresholds have not yet received agronomic validation, and farmers should continue to consult local agricultural experts and verify field conditions.

Our Vision

We want to make Earth observation technology understandable and useful beyond research laboratories.

Safe Field Nepal represents our effort to connect NASA's view of Earth from space with the knowledge and everyday experiences of farmers on the ground.

Better information. Smarter decisions. Stronger farming communities.
